transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Whitfield. This is your six-month check on the atrial fibrillation. How have you been feeling?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Pretty good. I notice my heart fluttering maybe once or twice a month, for a few minutes, and then it settles.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any shortness of breath, fainting, or swelling in your legs?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No. I still walk the dog every morning, about a mile.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: You're on apixaban 5 mg twice a day and metoprolol succinate 50 mg once a day. Any bleeding?

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: No nosebleeds, blood in the urine, or dark stools?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No. Well, my gums bleed a little when I brush, I guess. It stops quickly.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: That's common on a blood thinner. Use a soft toothbrush and mention it to your dentist. Have you missed any apixaban doses?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I use a pill box.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Your heart rate is 72 and irregularly irregular, blood pressure is 128 over 78. Lungs are clear, and there's no leg edema.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Your atrial fibrillation is well rate controlled with only brief, infrequent palpitations. We'll continue apixaban 5 mg twice a day and metoprolol succinate 50 mg once a day. I'll order blood work, a complete blood count and a kidney panel, to make sure the apixaban dose is still right.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay. Anything I should watch for?

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Call us if the fluttering lasts more than an hour or you feel faint. Go to the emergency department for black stools, vomiting blood, or any bleeding that won't stop. We'll see you again in six months.

sections.title: Interval history
sections.text: Heart fluttering once or twice a month for a few minutes, then settles. No shortness of breath, fainting, or leg swelling. Walks the dog about a mile every morning. On apixaban 5 mg twice a day and metoprolol succinate 50 mg once a day; uses a pill box, no missed doses. Gums bleed a little when he brushes and it stops quickly; no nosebleeds, no blood in the urine, no dark stools.

sections.title: Physical exam
sections.text: Heart rate 72, irregularly irregular. Blood pressure 128/78. Lungs clear. No leg edema.

sections.title: Assessment and plan
sections.text: Atrial fibrillation, well rate controlled, with brief, infrequent palpitations. Continue apixaban 5 mg twice a day and metoprolol succinate 50 mg once a day. Complete blood count and kidney panel to check the apixaban dose. Gum bleeding when brushing: soft toothbrush, mention it to the dentist. Follow-up in six months.

sections.title: Patient instructions
sections.text: Keep taking apixaban 5 mg twice a day and metoprolol succinate 50 mg once a day. Use a soft toothbrush and mention the gum bleeding to your dentist. Call us if the fluttering lasts more than an hour or you feel faint. Go to the emergency department for black stools, vomiting blood, or bleeding that won't stop. Return in six months.

mustNotInvent.description: No other blood thinner was discussed.
No echocardiogram or ECG was ordered.
Dizziness and chest pain were not reported.

conflicts.description: He first says no bleeding, then mentions his gums bleed a little when brushing.
